newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Japan's Sony upbeat on multimedia earnings.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Sony upbeat on multimedia earnings.

text.p: Sony Corp. officials predicted Friday that the group's foray into mixing consumer electronics and computer features into multimedia products would generate huge contributions to its earnings.

"We have research and development activity in the U.S. and in Europe for the multimedia area. It will have an enormous contribution in the long term," said Suehiro Nakamura, Sony's managing director and president of its display company.
Officials in Singapore and Japan were not able to say how much Sony had invested or intends to invest in multimedia products.

Sony began selling so-called Web televisions last October in the United States, officials said. Web television is a terminal that lets users access the Internet and display the content on a television set. It also has electronic mail capability.
"Soon in 1998, we will have a similar system in Japan," Nakamura told reporters at a briefing, adding that Sony could also sell Web TV in Europe in the near future.

Nakamura said Sony had also ventured into interactive television in Japan that is named IT TV. It allows users to receive information from broadcasters and then contact broadcasters through telephone cables, he said.
Sony has said its move into such products was spurred by the increased convergence of computers and consumer electronics.
Nakamura said Sony had also been successful in its recent launch of personal computers in the United States.

Sony's PCs, which combine the company's audio and visual capabilities, are targeted at the consumer market, he said. Since its launch in October last year, Sony has sold 300,000 PCs in the United States, officials said.
For the half year ended September 1996, Sony reported its group net profit more then tripled to 51.74 billion yen ($442 million) on sales of 2.53 trillion yen ($21.6 billion).
Sony has forecast net profit of 105 billion yen ($897 million) for the full year ending March 1997 on projected sales of 5.35 trillion yen ($45.7 billion).
